clue.text: March is when he does his show

definitions.text: March is when he does his show

parts.words: March is when he does his show
parts.note: a march is a protest procession, so the person who goes on one shows their views by marching rather than performing

explanation.surface: Someone who stages his show every year in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is the protest walk, and 'show' is the showing of an opinion on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester taking part in a march is a marcher showing support for a cause.

clue.text: Successfully rival bird -teal perhaps

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word teal could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: One bird, a teal perhaps, competing well against another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TEAL into LATE, which follows EMU.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to match or equal their achievements by imitation.

clue.text: Gloomy situation of theatrical producer?

definitions.meaning: dull and cloudy, describing a grey sky
a producer is placed in charge, above the actors in the play, the question mark flagging the split reading

explanation.definitionFit: A dark sky is clouded over, while a producer stands over the actors hired for a show.

clue.text: When to keep quiet about waistband

indicators.note: about means the hush sound goes around the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call telling someone to keep quiet
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Asking at what point one should stop talking about a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SH around AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn around the middle, a type of belt.

clue.text: Soldier made every effort to appear controlled

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords
strained means tried as hard as possible

explanation.surface: A soldier pushed himself hard so as to look composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in check or showing calm self-control is reserved and measured.

clue.text: Rates varied due to weeds…

indicators.note: varied means the letters of rates are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Charges changed because of unwanted plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tares are the weeds sown among wheat in the biblical parable.

clue.text: … round one domed build

parts.note: rotund means round or plump
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: Continuing from the weeds clue: a round building with a dome.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, typically topped with a dome.

clue.text: Coin only 50% royal

parts.note: fifty per cent is a half
a sovereign is a king or queen

explanation.surface: A coin worth only half as much as the royal one.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-sovereign was an old British gold coin worth ten shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: This old gold coin was worth half of a pound-valued gold piece.

clue.text: Strange man embracing girl followed by crowd of US journalists

indicators.note: followed by puts the next piece after the first
embracing means the scrambled letters go round the girl's name
strange means the letters of man appear in an unusual order

parts.note: Erica is a girl's name
press means a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: An odd man holding a girl, then a crowd of reporters from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns MAN into AMN, and 'embracing' puts ERICA inside it, after AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspapers and reporters of the United States collectively form its media.

clue.text: Mulled ale must have charms

indicators.note: mulled means heated and spiced, so the letters of ale must are stirred up

explanation.surface: A warm spiced drink of ale must have its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mulled' rearranges ALE MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Amulets are lucky charms worn to ward off harm.

clue.text: Layer-cakes turned out by backsliding churchwomen

indicators.note: turned out, as cakes turned out of a tin, signals the letters being shaken into a new order

parts.note: tarts are small pastry cakes

indicators.note: backsliding means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MU is the Mothers' Union, a Church of England women's organisation

explanation.surface: Layer cakes baked by churchwomen who have lapsed in their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges TARTS to STRAT, and 'backsliding' turns MU into UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is one level of rock or of society.

clue.text: Managed football club without foreign money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the club's letters go around

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A manager ran a football club that was short of foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so FC surrounds RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and remains that of Switzerland.

clue.text: One who is captivated by a sentence?

definitions.text: One who is captivated by a sentence?

parts.words: One who is captivated by a sentence?
parts.note: captivated is read as made captive and the sentence is a court's, not a line of writing

explanation.surface: Someone enchanted by a well-made line of words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated' looks like charmed but means held captive, and 'sentence' is the punishment a judge passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict serving time in jail has been locked up under a judge's ruling.

clue.text: Hermaphrodite calf unimpeded by bird

parts.note: free means unhindered or unimpeded
the martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A calf of both sexes allowed to roam among birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A freemartin is a sterile female calf born twin to a male.
explanation.definitionFit: A freemartin is a sexually imperfect heifer, twinned with a bull calf.

clue.text: Result of too much pressure for deliveries by rail

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
a train runs on rail

explanation.surface: Excess pressure caused by sending goods by railway.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive stress or tension on a body or material leaves it damaged and overworked.

clue.text: Mineral in metal container

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the words metal container

explanation.surface: A mineral stored in a tin box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run inside 'meTAL Container'.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft magnesium silicate mineral used for talcum powder.

clue.text: Cultivate way-out sets but remain superlatively calm

indicators.note: way-out means wild or eccentric, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: till means to cultivate the soil

explanation.surface: Tending eccentric stage sets while keeping perfectly calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' rearranges TILL plus SETS; 'but remain' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillest is the superlative of still, meaning the most motionless or tranquil.

clue.text: Painter of cabinet types

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from inside the words cabinet types

explanation.surface: An artist who designs kinds of cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to the run inside 'cabinET TYpes'; William Etty was a 19th-century English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English artist noted for his nude figure paintings.

clue.text: Boy singer's first descant in triplicate

parts.note: a treble is a boy with a high singing voice

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of descant

explanation.surface: A choirboy sings his first descant three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes D from 'descant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made three times as great or repeated threefold has been tripled.

clue.text: Prosaic footman

definitions.meaning: one who travels on foot, a walker

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dull and unimaginative and a person walking rather than riding.

clue.text: Draw negative conclusion from conflagration

parts.note: to draw a conclusion is to infer
no is a negative answer or verdict

explanation.surface: Concluding something bad from a great blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large, uncontrollable fire.

clue.text: Final turn to a novice after race

indicators.note: after puts the race before the other pieces

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
a U-turn makes U stand for turn
L is the learner plate sign for a novice driver

explanation.surface: A last bend for a beginner after the race.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands for turn, from U-turn, and L for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means ultimate, happening at the end of a process.

clue.text: Object to night-work

indicators.note: work means the letters of night are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Raising a protest about doing night shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an item or object.

clue.text: Long-term prisoner's file reviewed by king

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again, so the letters of file are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king looks over the dossier of a prisoner serving many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges FILE to LIFE, then R for king follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence is held for a very long term.

clue.text: Employer getting custom right

parts.note: use means custom or habit, as in 'by long use'

explanation.surface: A boss who gains regular trade fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: Soldier getting everyone to go back to ship

indicators.note: getting means the soldier takes in the next piece

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
all means everyone

indicators.note: go back means the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A soldier rallying everyone to return to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' puts ALL inside GI, and 'go back' turns TO into OT. A galliot is a light Dutch cargo ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galliot is a small galley or Dutch trading vessel.

clue.text: One mistake -taking specialist force round mountain range

definitions.note: singular in the clue, while the answer is plural: each one is a jagged chain of peaks

indicators.note: round means the force's letters go around the others

parts.note: SAS is the Special Air Service, a British special forces regiment
I is the Roman numeral one
err means to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone making a blunder involving special forces in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts SAS around I and ERR. The plural sierras names the peaks of one range, as in the Sierra Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged chain of peaks, a Spanish word used for such ranges.

clue.text: Falling off of French production

parts.note: de is the French word for of
generation means production, as in generation of power

explanation.surface: A slump in output from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Decline or deterioration in quality is a falling away from a former standard.
